question: Does parallel attention/FFN residual composition with separate RMSNorms improve the adopted D256 MLA tokenizer recipe at fixed peak LR0.00125?

architecture_review.selected: Parallel separate-norm residual topology versus serial
architecture_review.rationale: Return to the explicitly queued residual-topology architecture question after the completed decay HP comparison. Parallel composition removes the within-block attention-to-FFN dependency without adding matrices, norms or cache state. This tests a dependency-graph change on the adopted subword MLA/blockRMS backbone, not another FFN activation or learning-rate search.
architecture_review.prior: The closed character MHA/LayerNorm study worsened every fresh seed and both widths; treat that as a negative prior, not a tokenizer result. Revisit only because tokenizer vocabulary/tables, attention compression, block normalization and1200-update horizon differ. No gain is assumed and no historical seed pooling.
